source.title: The Wedding Style Guide: It's not about you
source.author: Permanent Style

tips.text: Treat a wedding as a chance to dress formally: a three-piece or double-breasted suit, a pocket square and a buttonhole.
tips.why: As business dress relaxes, weddings are one of the last natural homes for the suit.

tips.text: At a wedding in a hot country, keep the tie but switch to a linen suit, and add a hat rather than resort to flip-flops.
tips.why: You stay smart while respecting the climate.

tips.text: Avoid bright suits, loud ties and socks, and tan shoes at a wedding.
tips.why: Elegance comes from cut, texture and restrained colour, not loudness.

tips.text: Choose a wedding suit that looks less like business wear, such as light grey or double-breasted.
tips.why: It marks the day as a special occasion.

tips.text: A navy suit looks less like office wear when it is double-breasted or in a textured cloth such as herringbone.
tips.why: Cut and texture take it away from the business uniform.

tips.text: Put a wedding outfit's colour into the pocket square and buttonhole rather than the tie or socks.
tips.why: Small accents add cheer while the core stays elegant.

tips.text: Skip anachronistic extras like tie bars and pocket watches with formal wedding wear.
tips.why: They look like dressing up rather than dressing well.

tips.text: Gauge a wedding's formality from the invitation, what you know of the hosts, or someone close to them; if in doubt, dress smartly.
tips.why: It's the hosts' event, and their expectations set the level.

tips.text: As a wedding guest, aim to fit in, not stand out; if people notice your outfit, you've probably misjudged it.
tips.why: Your job is to honour the hosts, not to be looked at.

tips.text: Follow a wedding's dress code even when it's unusual, such as black tie in the daytime or beachwear.
tips.why: Respecting the hosts' wishes matters more than convention.

tips.text: When accompanying a partner to a wedding, dress to complement her outfit rather than compete with it.
tips.why: Neither of you should outshine the bride.
